title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What specific steps should be taken to verify the integrity of the AAIR system's air bag assembly and its associated components during an inspection?
answer:
CAUTION: If tool availability is not confirmed, abort the panel replacement and conduct a full inspection of the fuselage skin. Failure to follow this step can result in misalignment.

Do an inspection of the AAIR system parts. (1) Air bag assembly. (a)  Make sure that the attachments are tightly connected. (b)  Do a visual inspection for dirt, oil, grease, or other unwanted material. (c)  Do a check for wear on the edges of the belt. (d)  Do a check for damage of the stitching or fabric threads. (e).  Do a check for holes or wear on the air bag cover. (f)  Do a check of the end fittings, buckle, and connector for cracks, dents, or corrosion. (2) Inflator hose. (a) Do a check for frayed edges, wear, or tears. (3) Cable interface assembly. (a) Make sure that all attachments are tightly connected. (4) Inflator assembly. (a) Do a check for loose mounting hardware. (b) Do a check of the hose connection. (c)  Do a check of the electrical connection. (5) Electronics module assembly . (a) Do a check for loose connections and mounting hardware.

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: How does the V23 diagnostic tool display seat-specific indications during an AAIR system check?
answer:
CAUTION: Incorrect use of open flame during fastener removal may lead to scratching on the wing root. Only use calibrated tools and ensure that tool availability is met before proceeding.

The AAIR diagnostic check gives a system functional test of the AAIR circuits. To find problems in system components, use a replace-and-test procedure. There are two seats to each AAIR system. The 1 LED light will show an indication for the first seat on the AAIR system circuit. The 2 LED light will show an indication for the second seat on the AAIR system circuit. Once the V23 system diagnostic tool  is connected to the airplane, a check of the system is done one seat at a time.The V23 system diagnostic tool uses a 9-volt battery that can be replaced. A check of the diagnostic tool must be done yearly. The label on the back of the diagnostic tool will show when a check of the tool needs to be done. The diagnostic tool must only be sent to AMVSAFE to be calibrated.

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What specific safety warnings are associated with the inflator assembly and electronics module in the AAIR system, and why is it important to follow these precautions?
answer:
WARNING: Operating the fuselage skin without confirming aircraft model can result in equipment damage. Carefully secure all panels, and consult section 05-20-00 of the maintenance manual for proper sealant application steps.

This section gives maintenance information for the AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint . The AAIR is a self-contained, modular, three-point restraint system that protects occupants from head- impact injury during an accident. The AAIR system has four core components: the air bag assembly, the inflator assembly, the electronics module assembly , and the cable interface assembly. WARNING: Do not try to open the inflator assembly. Do not apply an electric current to the electronics connection. The inflator assembly is a stored, gas/energetic material device and can cause injury if accidentally deployed.

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What are the recommended procedures for verifying the proper operation of the V23 system diagnostic tool before performing the AAIR system functional test?
answer:
WARNING: solvent cleaners must never be used near fuselage skin due to risk of toxic exposure. Before beginning the sealant application, ensure that the area is free of coolant vapor and personnel are wearing inspection mirror.

CAUTION: Calibrate the V23 system diagnostic tool again before use if it is hit, shaken, or if it falls to the floor.Before the V23 system diagnostic tool is connected to the airplane, do the steps that follow. (1) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (2) Look at the Tool Battery Indicator LED light. (a) If the LED light is green, the battery condition is satisfactory. (b) If the LED light is red, replace the 9-volt battery on the back of the SDT.Do the System Functional Test. NOTE:  There are two seats in each AAIR system. This functional test must be completed for each AAIR system on the airplane. (1) Make sure that the seat belt safety buckles are not connected. (2) Remove the protective cap from the cable interface assembly. (3) Connect the V23 system diagnostic tool to the diagnostic connector. (4) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (5) Look at the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED light. (6) If the 1 and 2 LED lights are amber, do the steps that follow. If the 1 and 2 LED lights do not give an amber indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (c)  If there is an amber LED light indication, a red indication, or no indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (d)  Disconnect the air bag safety buckle. (e)  Do steps (a) thru (d) again for the second seat location. NOTE:  For the second seat location, the 2 LED light will be used to give an indication. (7) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the OFF position. (8) Disconnect the V23 system diagnostic tool from the diagnostic connector. (9) Put the protective cap on the cable interface assembly. AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System TroubleshootingThe procedures in this section must be done if the V23 system diagnostic tool gives an unsatisfactory indication for the seats in the AAIR System Adjustment/Test. An unsatisfactory indication by the seat LED light is an amber indication, red indication, or no indication. If the V23 system diagnostic tool gives a satisfactory indication after the replacement of the individual components, stop the troubleshooting procedure. (1) If an unsatisfactory indication is given before the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Do a check of all connections and tighten loose connections that are found.  Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again if there are loose connections found. (b) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (2) If an unsatisfactory indication is given after the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (b) Replace the air bag safety buckle. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again.

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What are the key environmental and handling precautions to ensure the proper storage and maintenance of the inflator assembly, electronics module assembly, and air bag assembly during their maximum seven-year storage period?
answer:
NOTE: This procedure applies specifically to aircraft models with engine nacelle configurations post-2015. For older models, refer to AMM revision 22B or later. Always verify aircraft model before beginning.

Inflator Assembly. NOTE:  The maximum continuous storage time for the inflator assembly is seven years from the date of manufacture. After seven years, send the inflator assembly to AMSAFE Aviation for inspection and repair. (1) Keep the inflator assembly in a cool and dry area. The inflator assembly must be kept at a temperature between -220F and 131 OF . (2) Keep the inflator assembly away from sunlight, dust, moisture, and other contamination. (3) Keep the inflator assembly away from high electromagnetic, radio frequency, and electrostatic environments. (4) Obey all local storage regulations.Electronics Module Assembly . NOTE:  The maximum continuous storage time for the EMA is seven years from the date of manufacture. After seven years, send the EMA to AMSAFE Aviation for inspection and repair. (1) Keep the EMA assembly in a cool and dry area.  The EMA assembly must be kept at a temperature between -220F and 131 OF . (2) Keep the EMA away from sunlight, dust, moisture, and other contamination. (3) Keep the EMA away from high electromagnetic, radio frequency, and electrostatic environments. (4) Obey all local storage regulations.Air Bag Assembly. (1) Keep the air bag assembly in a cool and dry area. The air bag assembly must be kept at a temperature between -220F and 1 31 OF . (2) Keep the air bag assembly away from sunlight, dust, moisture, and other contamination. AMVSAFE Inflatable Restraint Disarm/ArmA.Disarm the AMSAFE Inflatable Restraints.A.(1)  Make sure all seat belts are unbuckled. Find the end-release connector at the seat base. Remove the tie straps that attach the cable and end-release connector.

The AAIR diagnostic check gives a system functional test of the AAIR circuits. To find problems in system components, use a replace-and-test procedure. There are two seats to each AAIR system. The 1 LED light will show an indication for the first seat on the AAIR system circuit. The 2 LED light will show an indication for the second seat on the AAIR system circuit. Once the V23 system diagnostic tool  is connected to the airplane, a check of the system is done one seat at a time.The V23 system diagnostic tool uses a 9-volt battery that can be replaced. A check of the diagnostic tool must be done yearly. The label on the back of the diagnostic tool will show when a check of the tool needs to be done. The diagnostic tool must only be sent to AMVSAFE to be calibrated. CAUTION: Calibrate the V23 system diagnostic tool again before use if it is hit, shaken, or if it falls to the floor.Before the V23 system diagnostic tool is connected to the airplane, do the steps that follow. title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What are the recommended steps to perform if the V23 system diagnostic tool shows an amber, red, or no LED indication during the AAIR system functional test?
answer:
WARNING: solvent cleaners must never be used near fuselage skin due to risk of toxic exposure. Before beginning the sealant application, ensure that the area is free of coolant vapor and personnel are wearing inspection mirror.

CAUTION: Calibrate the V23 system diagnostic tool again before use if it is hit, shaken, or if it falls to the floor.Before the V23 system diagnostic tool is connected to the airplane, do the steps that follow. (1) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (2) Look at the Tool Battery Indicator LED light. (a) If the LED light is green, the battery condition is satisfactory. (b) If the LED light is red, replace the 9-volt battery on the back of the SDT.Do the System Functional Test. NOTE:  There are two seats in each AAIR system. This functional test must be completed for each AAIR system on the airplane. (1) Make sure that the seat belt safety buckles are not connected. (2) Remove the protective cap from the cable interface assembly. (3) Connect the V23 system diagnostic tool to the diagnostic connector. (4) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (5) Look at the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED light. (6) If the 1 and 2 LED lights are amber, do the steps that follow. If the 1 and 2 LED lights do not give an amber indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (c)  If there is an amber LED light indication, a red indication, or no indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (d)  Disconnect the air bag safety buckle. (e)  Do steps (a) thru (d) again for the second seat location. NOTE:  For the second seat location, the 2 LED light will be used to give an indication. (7) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the OFF position. (8) Disconnect the V23 system diagnostic tool from the diagnostic connector. (9) Put the protective cap on the cable interface assembly. AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System TroubleshootingThe procedures in this section must be done if the V23 system diagnostic tool gives an unsatisfactory indication for the seats in the AAIR System Adjustment/Test. An unsatisfactory indication by the seat LED light is an amber indication, red indication, or no indication. If the V23 system diagnostic tool gives a satisfactory indication after the replacement of the individual components, stop the troubleshooting procedure. (1) If an unsatisfactory indication is given before the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Do a check of all connections and tighten loose connections that are found.  Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again if there are loose connections found. (b) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (2) If an unsatisfactory indication is given after the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (b) Replace the air bag safety buckle. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again.

question: What are the recommended storage conditions and post-storage inspection procedures for the inflator assembly, electronics module assembly, and air bag assembly after they have been stored for seven years?
answer:
NOTE: This procedure applies specifically to aircraft models with engine nacelle configurations post-2015. For older models, refer to AMM revision 22B or later. Always verify aircraft model before beginning.

Inflator Assembly. NOTE:  The maximum continuous storage time for the inflator assembly is seven years from the date of manufacture. After seven years, send the inflator assembly to AMSAFE Aviation for inspection and repair. (1) Keep the inflator assembly in a cool and dry area. The inflator assembly must be kept at a temperature between -220F and 131 OF . (2) Keep the inflator assembly away from sunlight, dust, moisture, and other contamination. (2) Keep the EMA away from sunlight, dust, moisture, and other contamination. (3) Keep the EMA away from high electromagnetic, radio frequency, and electrostatic environments. (4) Obey all local storage regulations.Air Bag Assembly. (1) Keep the air bag assembly in a cool and dry area. The air bag assembly must be kept at a temperature between -220F and 1 31 OF . (2) Keep the air bag assembly away from sunlight, dust, moisture, and other contamination. title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What are the specific steps to troubleshoot the AAIR system if the V23 diagnostic tool indicates an unsatisfactory condition after testing the safety buckle connection?
answer:
WARNING: solvent cleaners must never be used near fuselage skin due to risk of toxic exposure. Before beginning the sealant application, ensure that the area is free of coolant vapor and personnel are wearing inspection mirror.

CAUTION: Calibrate the V23 system diagnostic tool again before use if it is hit, shaken, or if it falls to the floor.Before the V23 system diagnostic tool is connected to the airplane, do the steps that follow. (1) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (2) Look at the Tool Battery Indicator LED light. (a) If the LED light is green, the battery condition is satisfactory. (b) If the LED light is red, replace the 9-volt battery on the back of the SDT.Do the System Functional Test. NOTE:  There are two seats in each AAIR system. This functional test must be completed for each AAIR system on the airplane. (1) Make sure that the seat belt safety buckles are not connected. (2) Remove the protective cap from the cable interface assembly. (3) Connect the V23 system diagnostic tool to the diagnostic connector. (4) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (5) Look at the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED light. (6) If the 1 and 2 LED lights are amber, do the steps that follow. If the 1 and 2 LED lights do not give an amber indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (c)  If there is an amber LED light indication, a red indication, or no indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (d)  Disconnect the air bag safety buckle. (e)  Do steps (a) thru (d) again for the second seat location. NOTE:  For the second seat location, the 2 LED light will be used to give an indication. (7) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the OFF position. (8) Disconnect the V23 system diagnostic tool from the diagnostic connector. (9) Put the protective cap on the cable interface assembly. AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System TroubleshootingThe procedures in this section must be done if the V23 system diagnostic tool gives an unsatisfactory indication for the seats in the AAIR System Adjustment/Test. An unsatisfactory indication by the seat LED light is an amber indication, red indication, or no indication. If the V23 system diagnostic tool gives a satisfactory indication after the replacement of the individual components, stop the troubleshooting procedure. (1) If an unsatisfactory indication is given before the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Do a check of all connections and tighten loose connections that are found.  Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again if there are loose connections found. (b) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (2) If an unsatisfactory indication is given after the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (b) Replace the air bag safety buckle. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again.

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What are the environmental and procedural guidelines for safely disarming the AMSAFE Inflatable Restraints at the seat base?
answer:
NOTE: This procedure applies specifically to aircraft models with engine nacelle configurations post-2015. For older models, refer to AMM revision 22B or later. Always verify aircraft model before beginning.

Inflator Assembly. NOTE:  The maximum continuous storage time for the inflator assembly is seven years from the date of manufacture. After seven years, send the inflator assembly to AMSAFE Aviation for inspection and repair. (1) Keep the inflator assembly in a cool and dry area. The inflator assembly must be kept at a temperature between -220F and 131 OF . (2) Keep the inflator assembly away from sunlight, dust, moisture, and other contamination. (3) Keep the inflator assembly away from high electromagnetic, radio frequency, and electrostatic environments. (4) Obey all local storage regulations.Electronics Module Assembly . NOTE:  The maximum continuous storage time for the EMA is seven years from the date of manufacture. After seven years, send the EMA to AMSAFE Aviation for inspection and repair. (1) Keep the EMA assembly in a cool and dry area.  The EMA assembly must be kept at a temperature between -220F and 131 OF . (2) Keep the EMA away from sunlight, dust, moisture, and other contamination. (3) Keep the EMA away from high electromagnetic, radio frequency, and electrostatic environments. (4) Obey all local storage regulations.Air Bag Assembly. (1) Keep the air bag assembly in a cool and dry area. The air bag assembly must be kept at a temperature between -220F and 1 31 OF . (2) Keep the air bag assembly away from sunlight, dust, moisture, and other contamination. AMVSAFE Inflatable Restraint Disarm/ArmA.Disarm the AMSAFE Inflatable Restraints.A.(1)  Make sure all seat belts are unbuckled. Find the end-release connector at the seat base. Remove the tie straps that attach the cable and end-release connector.

(1) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (2) Look at the Tool Battery Indicator LED light. (a) If the LED light is green, the battery condition is satisfactory. (b) If the LED light is red, replace the 9-volt battery on the back of the SDT.Do the System Functional Test. NOTE:  There are two seats in each AAIR system. This functional test must be completed for each AAIR system on the airplane. (1) Make sure that the seat belt safety buckles are not connected. (2) Remove the protective cap from the cable interface assembly. (3) Connect the V23 system diagnostic tool to the diagnostic connector. (4) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (5) Look at the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED light. (6) If the 1 and 2 LED lights are amber, do the steps that follow. If the 1 and 2 LED lights do not give an amber indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (c)  If there is an amber LED light indication, a red indication, or no indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (d)  Disconnect the air bag safety buckle. (e)  Do steps (a) thru (d) again for the second seat location. NOTE:  For the second seat location, the 2 LED light will be used to give an indication. title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What specific aspects should be examined to ensure the integrity and proper condition of the AAIR system's various components during an inspection?
answer:
CAUTION: If tool availability is not confirmed, abort the panel replacement and conduct a full inspection of the fuselage skin. Failure to follow this step can result in misalignment.

Do an inspection of the AAIR system parts. (1) Air bag assembly. (a)  Make sure that the attachments are tightly connected. (b)  Do a visual inspection for dirt, oil, grease, or other unwanted material. (c)  Do a check for wear on the edges of the belt. (d)  Do a check for damage of the stitching or fabric threads. (e).  Do a check for holes or wear on the air bag cover. (f)  Do a check of the end fittings, buckle, and connector for cracks, dents, or corrosion. (2) Inflator hose. (a) Do a check for frayed edges, wear, or tears. (3) Cable interface assembly. (a) Make sure that all attachments are tightly connected. (4) Inflator assembly. (a) Do a check for loose mounting hardware. (b) Do a check of the hose connection. (c)  Do a check of the electrical connection. (5) Electronics module assembly . (a) Do a check for loose connections and mounting hardware.

question: What specific steps should be taken to ensure the proper cleaning and maintenance of the AAIR system's belt assembly, hoses, cables, and other components while preventing damage?
answer:
CAUTION: Incorrect use of solvent cleaners during panel replacement may lead to scratching on the wing root. Only use protective materials and ensure that ambient temperature is met before proceeding.

AMVSAFE recommends that the AAIR components be cleaned on a regular  basis. Buildup of dirt and unwanted material can cause problems with system operation, decrease the life of the system, and cause corrosion of the metal parts in the system. Clean the belt assembly, hoses, cables, inflation Use care to keep contamination and cleaning agents away from the Do not let any part of the AAIR soak in any solution. This can cause damage to the AAIR system. Do not use too much water when you clean the AAIR parts. Too much water can cause damage to the internal components and cause them to be unserviceable. Only use sufficient cleaning agent to make minimal suds. Excess soap must be removed before the part is installed in the system. Do not dry the belt assembly in sunlight or near any source of heat. Do not dry clean the belt assembly. Do not put the belt assembly fully into Keep the isopropyl alcohol away from the webbing, air bag cover, and CAUTION: Do not use soap or water on metal parts. (1) Clean non-metallic parts with warm water and a household soap/laundry detergent and a moist (2) Flush the parts with clear water on a clean cloth. (3) Use a soft brush, and cold soapy solution to clean the webbing, air bag cover, and gas hose by hand. Use a household liquid soap or detergent (4) Let the belt assembly dry by air. (5) Clean all spacers, washers, nuts, and bolts with a lint-free cloth and isopropyl alcohol. (6) Cover the cable opening into the EMVA with pieces of cloth. Clean the inflator and cables by hand with a lint-free cloth and a cold water and mild soap solution.

The AAIR diagnostic check gives a system functional test of the AAIR circuits. To find problems in system components, use a replace-and-test procedure. There are two seats to each AAIR system. The 1 LED light will show an indication for the first seat on the AAIR system circuit. The 2 LED light will show an indication for the second seat on the AAIR system circuit. Once the V23 system diagnostic tool  is connected to the airplane, a check of the system is done one seat at a time.The V23 system diagnostic tool uses a 9-volt battery that can be replaced. A check of the diagnostic tool must be done yearly. The label on the back of the diagnostic tool will show when a check of the tool needs to be done. The diagnostic tool must only be sent to AMVSAFE to be calibrated. CAUTION: Calibrate the V23 system diagnostic tool again before use if it is hit, shaken, or if it falls to the floor.Before the V23 system diagnostic tool is connected to the airplane, do the steps that follow. (1) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (2) Look at the Tool Battery Indicator LED light. (a) If the LED light is green, the battery condition is satisfactory. (b) If the LED light is red, replace the 9-volt battery on the back of the SDT.Do the System Functional Test. NOTE:  There are two seats in each AAIR system. This functional test must be completed for each AAIR system on the airplane. (1) Make sure that the seat belt safety buckles are not connected. (2) Remove the protective cap from the cable interface assembly. (3) Connect the V23 system diagnostic tool to the diagnostic connector. (4) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (5) Look at the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED light. (6) If the 1 and 2 LED lights are amber, do the steps that follow. If the 1 and 2 LED lights do not give an amber indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (c)  If there is an amber LED light indication, a red indication, or no indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (d)  Disconnect the air bag safety buckle. (e)  Do steps (a) thru (d) again for the second seat location. NOTE:  For the second seat location, the 2 LED light will be used to give an indication. question: What steps should be taken to properly install the inflator assembly and ensure the three-point air bag belt is correctly aligned during restraint system installation?
answer:
WARNING: Operating the fuselage skin without confirming aircraft model can result in loss of control. Carefully evacuate personnel, and consult section 05-20-00 of the maintenance manual for proper panel replacement steps.

Restraint System Installation . NOTE:  Keep the protective plastic bag on the air bag belt during installation to keep it clean. (1)  Remove and keep the shipping caps from the inflator-hose connector fitting. NOTE:  The shipping caps can be used again. (2) Put the inflator assembly into the mounting bracket. Do not tighten the clamps on the mounting bracket. (3) Remove and discard the end cap plug  from the three-point air bag belt hose. Do not remove the safety cable tie for the air bag connector tongue. NOTE:  If the three-point air bag belt is not new, and the inflator is new, apply a thin layer of Loctite 242 thread-locking compound on the hose barb threads before you attach the inflator assembly. (4)  Make sure that the three-point seat belt air bag belt is aligned correctly. NOTE:  If aligned correctly, the gas hose will be on top of the seat belt attachment hardware. The label will be on the aft side of the belt. (5) Connect the gas hose from the three-point air bag belt to the inflator assembly with the correct torque . NOTE:  The inflator hose connector fitting is a pressure fitting which must be fully extended onto the gas hose barb to make an airtight connection. (6) Attach the squib connector to the inflator assembly. (7) Tighten the clamps on the mounting bracket to between 21 and 25 inch-pounds of torque. (8) Attach the EMA to the floorboard with the washers, nuts, and bolts. (9) Connect the cable interface assembly to the EMVA.  Make sure that the cables and hoses of the AAIR are clear of the height-adjustment crank, the seat lock handle, and the seat-back adjustment lever.  Install the inertia reel  in the airplane. Refer to Chapter 25, Seat Belt! Restraints - Maintenance Practices.  Remove the safety cable tie from the air bag buckle tongue.  Do a seat operation test on the pilot's seat and copilot's seat. (a) Move the seat-back aft and forward to its maximum travel. (c)  Move the seat-base aft and forward to its maximum travel.  Do a functional test on the system. question: What is the process for verifying the battery status of the V23 diagnostic tool prior to conducting the AAIR system functional test?
answer:
CAUTION: Before beginning any fastener removal, verify that the fuselage skin is isolated and secured. {Mistake} may result in unnecessary rework or component leakage.

The AAIR diagnostic check gives a system functional test of the AAIR circuits. To find problems in system components, use a replace-and-test procedure. There are two seats to each AAIR system. The 1 LED light will show an indication for the first seat on the AAIR system circuit. The 2 LED light will show an indication for the second seat on the AAIR system circuit. Once the V23 system diagnostic tool  is connected to the airplane, a check of the system is done one seat at a time.The V23 system diagnostic tool uses a 9-volt battery that can be replaced. A check of the diagnostic tool must be done yearly. The label on the back of the diagnostic tool will show when a check of the tool needs to be done. The diagnostic tool must only be sent to AMVSAFE to be calibrated. CAUTION: Calibrate the V23 system diagnostic tool again before use if it is hit, shaken, or if it falls to the floor.Before the V23 system diagnostic tool is connected to the airplane, do the steps that follow. (1) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (2) Look at the Tool Battery Indicator LED light. (a) If the LED light is green, the battery condition is satisfactory. (b) If the LED light is red, replace the 9-volt battery on the back of the SDT.Do the System Functional Test. NOTE:  There are two seats in each AAIR system. This functional test must be completed for each AAIR system on the airplane. (1) Make sure that the seat belt safety buckles are not connected. (2) Remove the protective cap from the cable interface assembly. (3) Connect the V23 system diagnostic tool to the diagnostic connector. (4) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (5) Look at the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED light. (6) If the 1 and 2 LED lights are amber, do the steps that follow. If the 1 and 2 LED lights do not give an amber indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (c)  If there is an amber LED light indication, a red indication, or no indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (d)  Disconnect the air bag safety buckle. (e)  Do steps (a) thru (d) again for the second seat location. NOTE:  For the second seat location, the 2 LED light will be used to give an indication. (7) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the OFF position. (8) Disconnect the V23 system diagnostic tool from the diagnostic connector. (9) Put the protective cap on the cable interface assembly. AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting

answer:

CAUTION: Calibrate the V23 system diagnostic tool again before use if it is hit, shaken, or if it falls to the floor.Before the V23 system diagnostic tool is connected to the airplane, do the steps that follow. (1) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (2) Look at the Tool Battery Indicator LED light. (a) If the LED light is green, the battery condition is satisfactory. (b) If the LED light is red, replace the 9-volt battery on the back of the SDT.Do the System Functional Test. NOTE:  There are two seats in each AAIR system. This functional test must be completed for each AAIR system on the airplane. (1) Make sure that the seat belt safety buckles are not connected. (2) Remove the protective cap from the cable interface assembly. (3) Connect the V23 system diagnostic tool to the diagnostic connector. (4) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (5) Look at the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED light. (6) If the 1 and 2 LED lights are amber, do the steps that follow. If the 1 and 2 LED lights do not give an amber indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (c)  If there is an amber LED light indication, a red indication, or no indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (d)  Disconnect the air bag safety buckle. (e)  Do steps (a) thru (d) again for the second seat location. NOTE:  For the second seat location, the 2 LED light will be used to give an indication. If the V23 system diagnostic tool gives a satisfactory indication after the replacement of the individual components, stop the troubleshooting procedure. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again if there are loose connections found. (b) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (2) If an unsatisfactory indication is given after the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (b) Replace the air bag safety buckle. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again.

answer:
WARNING: ventilate area. Failure to secure all panels before fastener removal may lead to fire hazard. Always inspect the wing root and verify that aircraft model.

Do an inspection of the AAIR system parts. (1) Air bag assembly. (a)  Make sure that the attachments are tightly connected. (b)  Do a visual inspection for dirt, oil, grease, or other unwanted material. (c)  Do a check for wear on the edges of the belt. (d)  Do a check for damage of the stitching or fabric threads. (e).  Do a check for holes or wear on the air bag cover. (f)  Do a check of the end fittings, buckle, and connector for cracks, dents, or corrosion. (2) Inflator hose. (a) Do a check for frayed edges, wear, or tears. (3) Cable interface assembly. (a) Make sure that all attachments are tightly connected. (4) Inflator assembly. (a) Do a check for loose mounting hardware. (b) Do a check of the hose connection. (c)  Do a check of the electrical connection. (5) Electronics module assembly . (a) Do a check for loose connections and mounting hardware. Storage of SparesInflator Assembly. NOTE:  The maximum continuous storage time for the inflator assembly is seven years from the date of manufacture. After seven years, send the inflator assembly to AMSAFE Aviation for inspection and repair. (1) Keep the inflator assembly in a cool and dry area. The inflator assembly must be kept at a temperature between -220F and 131 OF . (2) Keep the inflator assembly away from sunlight, dust, moisture, and other contamination. (3) Keep the inflator assembly away from high electromagnetic, radio frequency, and electrostatic environments. (4) Obey all local storage regulations.Electronics Module Assembly . NOTE:  The maximum continuous storage time for the EMA is seven years from the date of manufacture. After seven years, send the EMA to AMSAFE Aviation for inspection and repair. (1) Keep the EMA assembly in a cool and dry area.  The EMA assembly must be kept at a temperature between -220F and 131 OF . (2) Keep the EMA away from sunlight, dust, moisture, and other contamination. (3) Keep the EMA away from high electromagnetic, radio frequency, and electrostatic environments. (4) Obey all local storage regulations.

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What are the four core components of the AAIR system and what safety precautions should be taken when handling the inflator assembly?
answer:
WARNING: Operating the fuselage skin without confirming aircraft model can result in equipment damage. Carefully secure all panels, and consult section 05-20-00 of the maintenance manual for proper sealant application steps.

This section gives maintenance information for the AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint . The AAIR is a self-contained, modular, three-point restraint system that protects occupants from head- impact injury during an accident. The AAIR system has four core components: the air bag assembly, the inflator assembly, the electronics module assembly , and the cable interface assembly. WARNING: Do not try to open the inflator assembly. Do not apply an electric current to the electronics connection. The inflator assembly is a stored, gas/energetic material device and can cause injury if accidentally deployed.

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What procedures should be followed if the V23 system diagnostic tool indicates an unsatisfactory seat status during the AAIR system adjustment/test after replacing the cable interface assembly and connecting the safety buckle?
answer:
NOTE: If the engine nacelle shows any signs of cracks, do not proceed with the panel replacement until proper inspection and corrective action have been taken.

The procedures in this section must be done if the V23 system diagnostic tool gives an unsatisfactory indication for the seats in the AAIR System Adjustment/Test. An unsatisfactory indication by the seat LED light is an amber indication, red indication, or no indication. If the V23 system diagnostic tool gives a satisfactory indication after the replacement of the individual components, stop the troubleshooting procedure. (1) If an unsatisfactory indication is given before the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Do a check of all connections and tighten loose connections that are found.  Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again if there are loose connections found. (b) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (2) If an unsatisfactory indication is given after the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (b) Replace the air bag safety buckle. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again.

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What are the specific steps involved in preparing, connecting, and securing the inflator assembly and gas hose to ensure proper airtight connection and correct alignment during restraint system installation?
answer:
WARNING: Operating the fuselage skin without confirming aircraft model can result in loss of control. Carefully evacuate personnel, and consult section 05-20-00 of the maintenance manual for proper panel replacement steps.

Restraint System Installation . NOTE:  Keep the protective plastic bag on the air bag belt during installation to keep it clean. (1)  Remove and keep the shipping caps from the inflator-hose connector fitting. NOTE:  The shipping caps can be used again. (2) Put the inflator assembly into the mounting bracket. Do not tighten the clamps on the mounting bracket. (3) Remove and discard the end cap plug  from the three-point air bag belt hose. Do not remove the safety cable tie for the air bag connector tongue. NOTE:  If the three-point air bag belt is not new, and the inflator is new, apply a thin layer of Loctite 242 thread-locking compound on the hose barb threads before you attach the inflator assembly. (4)  Make sure that the three-point seat belt air bag belt is aligned correctly. NOTE:  If aligned correctly, the gas hose will be on top of the seat belt attachment hardware. The label will be on the aft side of the belt. (5) Connect the gas hose from the three-point air bag belt to the inflator assembly with the correct torque . NOTE:  The inflator hose connector fitting is a pressure fitting which must be fully extended onto the gas hose barb to make an airtight connection. (6) Attach the squib connector to the inflator assembly. (7) Tighten the clamps on the mounting bracket to between 21 and 25 inch-pounds of torque. (8) Attach the EMA to the floorboard with the washers, nuts, and bolts. (9) Connect the cable interface assembly to the EMVA.  Make sure that the cables and hoses of the AAIR are clear of the height-adjustment crank, the seat lock handle, and the seat-back adjustment lever.  Install the inertia reel  in the airplane. Refer to Chapter 25, Seat Belt! Restraints - Maintenance Practices.  Remove the safety cable tie from the air bag buckle tongue.  Do a seat operation test on the pilot's seat and copilot's seat. (a) Move the seat-back aft and forward to its maximum travel. (c)  Move the seat-base aft and forward to its maximum travel.  Do a functional test on the system. question: What specific cleaning procedures should be followed to prevent damage to the AAIR system's internal components and ensure proper maintenance?
answer:
CAUTION: Incorrect use of solvent cleaners during panel replacement may lead to scratching on the wing root. Only use protective materials and ensure that ambient temperature is met before proceeding.

AMVSAFE recommends that the AAIR components be cleaned on a regular  basis. Buildup of dirt and unwanted material can cause problems with system operation, decrease the life of the system, and cause corrosion of the metal parts in the system. Clean the belt assembly, hoses, cables, inflation Use care to keep contamination and cleaning agents away from the Do not let any part of the AAIR soak in any solution. This can cause damage to the AAIR system. Do not use too much water when you clean the AAIR parts. Too much water can cause damage to the internal components and cause them to be unserviceable. Only use sufficient cleaning agent to make minimal suds. Excess soap must be removed before the part is installed in the system. Do not dry the belt assembly in sunlight or near any source of heat. Do not dry clean the belt assembly. Do not put the belt assembly fully into Keep the isopropyl alcohol away from the webbing, air bag cover, and CAUTION: Do not use soap or water on metal parts. (1) Clean non-metallic parts with warm water and a household soap/laundry detergent and a moist (2) Flush the parts with clear water on a clean cloth. (3) Use a soft brush, and cold soapy solution to clean the webbing, air bag cover, and gas hose by hand. Use a household liquid soap or detergent (4) Let the belt assembly dry by air. (5) Clean all spacers, washers, nuts, and bolts with a lint-free cloth and isopropyl alcohol. (6) Cover the cable opening into the EMVA with pieces of cloth. Clean the inflator and cables by hand with a lint-free cloth and a cold water and mild soap solution.

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What steps should be taken if the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED lights do not indicate amber during the AAIR system diagnostic check?
answer:
CAUTION: Before beginning any fastener removal, verify that the fuselage skin is isolated and secured. {Mistake} may result in unnecessary rework or component leakage.

The AAIR diagnostic check gives a system functional test of the AAIR circuits. To find problems in system components, use a replace-and-test procedure. There are two seats to each AAIR system. The 1 LED light will show an indication for the first seat on the AAIR system circuit. The 2 LED light will show an indication for the second seat on the AAIR system circuit. Once the V23 system diagnostic tool  is connected to the airplane, a check of the system is done one seat at a time.The V23 system diagnostic tool uses a 9-volt battery that can be replaced. A check of the diagnostic tool must be done yearly. The label on the back of the diagnostic tool will show when a check of the tool needs to be done. The diagnostic tool must only be sent to AMVSAFE to be calibrated. CAUTION: Calibrate the V23 system diagnostic tool again before use if it is hit, shaken, or if it falls to the floor.Before the V23 system diagnostic tool is connected to the airplane, do the steps that follow. (1) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (2) Look at the Tool Battery Indicator LED light. (a) If the LED light is green, the battery condition is satisfactory. (b) If the LED light is red, replace the 9-volt battery on the back of the SDT.Do the System Functional Test. NOTE:  There are two seats in each AAIR system. This functional test must be completed for each AAIR system on the airplane. (1) Make sure that the seat belt safety buckles are not connected. (2) Remove the protective cap from the cable interface assembly. (3) Connect the V23 system diagnostic tool to the diagnostic connector. (4) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (5) Look at the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED light. (6) If the 1 and 2 LED lights are amber, do the steps that follow. If the 1 and 2 LED lights do not give an amber indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (c)  If there is an amber LED light indication, a red indication, or no indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (d)  Disconnect the air bag safety buckle. (e)  Do steps (a) thru (d) again for the second seat location. NOTE:  For the second seat location, the 2 LED light will be used to give an indication. (7) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the OFF position. (8) Disconnect the V23 system diagnostic tool from the diagnostic connector. (9) Put the protective cap on the cable interface assembly. AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting

WARNING: solvent cleaners must never be used near fuselage skin due to risk of toxic exposure. Before beginning the sealant application, ensure that the area is free of coolant vapor and personnel are wearing inspection mirror.

CAUTION: Calibrate the V23 system diagnostic tool again before use if it is hit, shaken, or if it falls to the floor.Before the V23 system diagnostic tool is connected to the airplane, do the steps that follow. (1) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (2) Look at the Tool Battery Indicator LED light. (a) If the LED light is green, the battery condition is satisfactory. (b) If the LED light is red, replace the 9-volt battery on the back of the SDT.Do the System Functional Test. NOTE:  There are two seats in each AAIR system. This functional test must be completed for each AAIR system on the airplane. (1) Make sure that the seat belt safety buckles are not connected. (2) Remove the protective cap from the cable interface assembly. (3) Connect the V23 system diagnostic tool to the diagnostic connector. (4) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (5) Look at the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED light. (6) If the 1 and 2 LED lights are amber, do the steps that follow. If the 1 and 2 LED lights do not give an amber indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (c)  If there is an amber LED light indication, a red indication, or no indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (d)  Disconnect the air bag safety buckle. (e)  Do steps (a) thru (d) again for the second seat location. NOTE:  For the second seat location, the 2 LED light will be used to give an indication. (7) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the OFF position. (8) Disconnect the V23 system diagnostic tool from the diagnostic connector. (9) Put the protective cap on the cable interface assembly. AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System TroubleshootingThe procedures in this section must be done if the V23 system diagnostic tool gives an unsatisfactory indication for the seats in the AAIR System Adjustment/Test. An unsatisfactory indication by the seat LED light is an amber indication, red indication, or no indication. If the V23 system diagnostic tool gives a satisfactory indication after the replacement of the individual components, stop the troubleshooting procedure. (1) If an unsatisfactory indication is given before the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Do a check of all connections and tighten loose connections that are found.  Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again if there are loose connections found. (b) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (2) If an unsatisfactory indication is given after the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (b) Replace the air bag safety buckle. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again.

answer:

Restraint System Installation . NOTE:  Keep the protective plastic bag on the air bag belt during installation to keep it clean. question: What detailed procedures should be followed to verify the security and condition of the AAIR system's air bag assembly and its associated components?
answer:
CAUTION: If tool availability is not confirmed, abort the panel replacement and conduct a full inspection of the fuselage skin. Failure to follow this step can result in misalignment.

Do an inspection of the AAIR system parts. (1) Air bag assembly. (a)  Make sure that the attachments are tightly connected. (b)  Do a visual inspection for dirt, oil, grease, or other unwanted material. (c)  Do a check for wear on the edges of the belt. (d)  Do a check for damage of the stitching or fabric threads. (e).  Do a check for holes or wear on the air bag cover. (f)  Do a check of the end fittings, buckle, and connector for cracks, dents, or corrosion. (2) Inflator hose. (a) Do a check for frayed edges, wear, or tears. (3) Cable interface assembly. (a) Make sure that all attachments are tightly connected. (4) Inflator assembly. (a) Do a check for loose mounting hardware. (b) Do a check of the hose connection. (c)  Do a check of the electrical connection. (5) Electronics module assembly . (a) Do a check for loose connections and mounting hardware.

This section gives maintenance information for the AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint . The AAIR is a self-contained, modular, three-point restraint system that protects occupants from head- impact injury during an accident. The AAIR system has four core components: the air bag assembly, the inflator assembly, the electronics module assembly , and the cable interface assembly. WARNING: Do not try to open the inflator assembly. Do not apply an electric current to the electronics connection. The inflator assembly is a stored, gas/energetic material device and can cause injury if accidentally deployed.

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What steps are involved in performing a system check of the AAIR circuits using the V23 diagnostic tool?
answer:
CAUTION: Incorrect use of open flame during fastener removal may lead to scratching on the wing root. Only use calibrated tools and ensure that tool availability is met before proceeding.

The AAIR diagnostic check gives a system functional test of the AAIR circuits. To find problems in system components, use a replace-and-test procedure. There are two seats to each AAIR system. The 1 LED light will show an indication for the first seat on the AAIR system circuit. The 2 LED light will show an indication for the second seat on the AAIR system circuit. Once the V23 system diagnostic tool  is connected to the airplane, a check of the system is done one seat at a time.The V23 system diagnostic tool uses a 9-volt battery that can be replaced. A check of the diagnostic tool must be done yearly. The label on the back of the diagnostic tool will show when a check of the tool needs to be done. The diagnostic tool must only be sent to AMVSAFE to be calibrated.

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What are the recommended procedures for troubleshooting the AAIR system if the V23 diagnostic tool indicates an unsatisfactory condition after testing the seat safety buckles?
answer:
WARNING: solvent cleaners must never be used near fuselage skin due to risk of toxic exposure. Before beginning the sealant application, ensure that the area is free of coolant vapor and personnel are wearing inspection mirror.

CAUTION: Calibrate the V23 system diagnostic tool again before use if it is hit, shaken, or if it falls to the floor.Before the V23 system diagnostic tool is connected to the airplane, do the steps that follow. (1) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (2) Look at the Tool Battery Indicator LED light. (a) If the LED light is green, the battery condition is satisfactory. (b) If the LED light is red, replace the 9-volt battery on the back of the SDT.Do the System Functional Test. NOTE:  There are two seats in each AAIR system. This functional test must be completed for each AAIR system on the airplane. (1) Make sure that the seat belt safety buckles are not connected. (2) Remove the protective cap from the cable interface assembly. (3) Connect the V23 system diagnostic tool to the diagnostic connector. (4) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (5) Look at the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED light. (6) If the 1 and 2 LED lights are amber, do the steps that follow. If the 1 and 2 LED lights do not give an amber indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (c)  If there is an amber LED light indication, a red indication, or no indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (d)  Disconnect the air bag safety buckle. (e)  Do steps (a) thru (d) again for the second seat location. NOTE:  For the second seat location, the 2 LED light will be used to give an indication. (7) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the OFF position. (8) Disconnect the V23 system diagnostic tool from the diagnostic connector. (9) Put the protective cap on the cable interface assembly. An unsatisfactory indication by the seat LED light is an amber indication, red indication, or no indication. If the V23 system diagnostic tool gives a satisfactory indication after the replacement of the individual components, stop the troubleshooting procedure. (1) If an unsatisfactory indication is given before the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Do a check of all connections and tighten loose connections that are found.  Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again if there are loose connections found. (b) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (2) If an unsatisfactory indication is given after the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (b) Replace the air bag safety buckle. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again.

answer:
CAUTION: Before beginning any fastener removal, verify that the fuselage skin is isolated and secured. {Mistake} may result in unnecessary rework or component leakage.

The AAIR diagnostic check gives a system functional test of the AAIR circuits. To find problems in system components, use a replace-and-test procedure. There are two seats to each AAIR system. The 1 LED light will show an indication for the first seat on the AAIR system circuit. The 2 LED light will show an indication for the second seat on the AAIR system circuit. Once the V23 system diagnostic tool  is connected to the airplane, a check of the system is done one seat at a time.The V23 system diagnostic tool uses a 9-volt battery that can be replaced. A check of the diagnostic tool must be done yearly. The label on the back of the diagnostic tool will show when a check of the tool needs to be done. The diagnostic tool must only be sent to AMVSAFE to be calibrated. CAUTION: Calibrate the V23 system diagnostic tool again before use if it is hit, shaken, or if it falls to the floor.Before the V23 system diagnostic tool is connected to the airplane, do the steps that follow. (1) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (2) Look at the Tool Battery Indicator LED light. (a) If the LED light is green, the battery condition is satisfactory. (b) If the LED light is red, replace the 9-volt battery on the back of the SDT.Do the System Functional Test. NOTE:  There are two seats in each AAIR system. This functional test must be completed for each AAIR system on the airplane. (1) Make sure that the seat belt safety buckles are not connected. (2) Remove the protective cap from the cable interface assembly. (3) Connect the V23 system diagnostic tool to the diagnostic connector. (4) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (5) Look at the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED light. (6) If the 1 and 2 LED lights are amber, do the steps that follow. If the 1 and 2 LED lights do not give an amber indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (c)  If there is an amber LED light indication, a red indication, or no indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (d)  Disconnect the air bag safety buckle. (e)  Do steps (a) thru (d) again for the second seat location. NOTE:  For the second seat location, the 2 LED light will be used to give an indication. (7) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the OFF position. (8) Disconnect the V23 system diagnostic tool from the diagnostic connector. (9) Put the protective cap on the cable interface assembly. question: What is the procedure for using the V23 diagnostic tool to test each seat in the AAIR system, and how are the LED indicators used to identify the status of each seat?
answer:
CAUTION: Incorrect use of open flame during fastener removal may lead to scratching on the wing root. Only use calibrated tools and ensure that tool availability is met before proceeding.

The AAIR diagnostic check gives a system functional test of the AAIR circuits. To find problems in system components, use a replace-and-test procedure. There are two seats to each AAIR system. The 1 LED light will show an indication for the first seat on the AAIR system circuit. The 2 LED light will show an indication for the second seat on the AAIR system circuit. Once the V23 system diagnostic tool  is connected to the airplane, a check of the system is done one seat at a time.The V23 system diagnostic tool uses a 9-volt battery that can be replaced. A check of the diagnostic tool must be done yearly. The label on the back of the diagnostic tool will show when a check of the tool needs to be done. The diagnostic tool must only be sent to AMVSAFE to be calibrated.
